packages.label: רוּחַ שְׁטוּת וְאֲוִיר
packages.reason: The source text explicitly equates ruach shtut (the spirit of folly) with avir (air), using the direct identity statement 'הָרוּחַ הוּא הָאֲוִיר' — 'the spirit IS the air.' This is the bechina-language identifier: ruach shtut and avir share the same essential nature; they are not cause and effect but two names for the same thing. The teaching's entire physical mechanism — that the spirit of folly pushes outward seeking an empty space to escape through, just as physical air does — depends on this identity. Together these two concepts form the evil/negative domain cluster: the antagonist force that fills a person's heart and must be expelled. Ruach shtut is the dominant node (it is named in the title of the Torah and drives the entire argument); avir is its physical-nature bechina, explaining why it behaves as it does.
